result.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the diff filters duplicates with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` — a strict case-sensitive comparison, with no lowercasing of either side. The client-side schema (`z.array(z.string().email())`) also doesn't normalize case, and the blacklist check lowercases only the blacklist, not the guest. So 'User@example.com' vs 'user@example.com' passes the dedup check and creates a duplicate attendee record, triggering duplicate emails. Mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication is done with a strict case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since neither side is normalized (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`), adding `Test@x.com` when `test@x.com` already exists will pass the filter and be treated as a new guest. The client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` similarly uses `new Set(emails)` without case normalization, so case variants can slip through end-to-end.
